title: Length-aware epochal batcher + KV saturation controller
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Summary: Mixed prompt/response workloads (chat + short prompts) cause inefficient continuous-batcher slot utilization and uneven KV residency on GPU memory. Short responses often coalesce quickly, while longer-turn assistants pin KV shards and prevent new high-priority short requests from meeting latency SLOs. This ticket implements an epochal batching layer that groups arrivals into short time-bounded 'epochs' with length-aware admission, combined with a KV saturation controller that proactively trims or demotes low-value KV entries and triggers spill-to-CPU for long-residency keys.

Goals: (1) Reduce p95 latency regression under mixed distributions by 10-20% for interactive (<=600ms target) classes; (2) Reduce GPU KV memory occupancy variance across windows (lower tail of free-GPU-memory by 30%); (3) Keep average throughput within 5% of current baseline for peak loads.

Design overview: The epochal batcher creates micro-epochs (configurable: 10-25ms) and assigns arriving requests into bins based on estimated combined length (prompt+expected response). We use a lightweight estimator in the ingress (token-length + historical response-multiplier per model) to classify into Short, Medium, Long bands. Within each epoch we perform two passes: (a) slot packing prioritizing short-band requests to meet hard latency SLOs, (b) opportunistic coalescing of medium/long items into background slots with preemption tokens. The KV saturation controller continuously monitors per-GPU KV residency metrics (entries, size, last_access_ts) and maintains a soft-saturation threshold. When soft-saturation is exceeded we run a trimming policy: demote prefix-only KV to compressed CPU cache, evict stale KV segments using a hybrid LFU-age heuristic, and optionally trigger kernel-level spill-to-CPU for specific shards.

Key mechanisms:
- Epoch windows: adjustable to workload skew; default 15ms.
- Length bands: Short(<64 tokens), Medium(64-512), Long(>512) — tunable per model.
- Preemption token budget per epoch: small integer (default 2) allowing background long requests to be started but yield if short requests arrive.
- KV saturation controller: hard and soft thresholds per GPU, histogram of residency time, demotion to compressed CPU hot-cache, and annotation so tracing can attribute evictions to specific service classes.
- Admission control: refuse or delay new very-long requests when both slot pressure and KV saturation are high (policy configurable by customer tier).

Why different from existing approaches: Rather than pure length-prioritized continuous coalescing, the epochal approach gives bounded decision points that reduce tail jitter due to asynchronous arrivals and enables deterministic preemption. The KV saturation controller focuses on 'value of residency' (recency + reuse probability) rather than pure LRU or time-based TTLs, improving memory signal for adaptive eviction.

Monitoring and observability: New metrics and traces: epoch_latency_p95/p50, epoch_slot_fill_ratio, kv_residency_histogram, kv_eviction_reasons, spill_to_cpu_ops, admission_block_rate. Dashboards and alert runbooks will be added under runtime-batching-2026 in Grafana/Console.

Rollout plan: Canary on testbed cluster (cpu-sim + 1 GPU) -> internal beta (10% traffic on staging) -> customer beta with opt-in and default off for lower tiers -> full rollout behind runtime-1.21 feature flag.
acceptance_criteria: p95 latency for short-band requests improves by >=10% under mixed load (validated with loadgen and production sampling)
GPU KV occupancy variance reduced by >=30% in histograms over 1-hour windows
No more than 5% drop in average throughput at 95th arrival percentile compared to baseline
End-to-end traces clearly show epoch boundaries and eviction reasons for KV entries
Automated canary tests and integration tests added to CI (loadgen harness, kv-sim)

Add ingress estimator for expected response length and classify into length bands
Implement KV saturation controller with demotion-to-CPU and hybrid LFU-age eviction
Add tracing hooks and metrics for epoch boundaries, slot decisions, and eviction reasons
Create unit + integration tests for preemption and admission control policies
Run simulations across synthetic mixes (chat-heavy, short-only, long-only, bursty interleaves)

Write design doc and add dashboard panels in Console runtime-batching-2026
comments: 2026-03-10 Maya Patel: Created ticket; initial design sketch after spike testing with loadgen. Observed p95 regressions when ~30% of requests are long (>512 tokens).
2026-03-11 Ethan Chen: Prototype epochal scheduler in local harness. 15ms epoch reduced jitter in synthetic mixed traces. Need to tune preemption budget — default 2 seems promising.
2026-03-12 Alex Rivera (review): Concern about eviction churn under high churn workloads; suggested hybrid LFU-age rather than pure LFU. Added as action item.
2026-03-13 SRE note (Jin Park): Canary must include KV eviction alerts and metric burn rate; suggested adding backoff window to avoid oscillation.
2026-03-14 Ethan Chen: KV saturation controller prototype integrated with tracer. Early sim shows 22% reduction in p95 for short-band under mixed load. Preparing PR and test vectors.
notes: Edge cases: server-side streaming responses complicate expected-length estimation; strategy is conservative classification for streams and permit longer preemption budgets.
Fallback: if eviction pressure becomes pathological, runtime should revert to existing continuous-batcher policy for that GPU for 60s and notify SRE.
Compatibility: make feature opt-out for Dedicated customers until validated with reserved capacity behavior.
